task_row_model.query: How can I read a binary stream in fixed-size chunks and decode it to UTF-8 strings in Python without splitting multibyte characters or raising UnicodeDecodeError?

documents.content: When reading arbitrary binary streams and converting to text, naive chunking risks slicing multi-byte UTF-8 sequences across chunk boundaries, which triggers UnicodeDecodeError if you call bytes.decode on an incomplete sequence. The standard solution is to use an incremental decoder that buffers incomplete sequences until they are complete. In Python that means creating a decoder from the codecs API, e.g. codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')(), then repeatedly call decoder.decode(chunk) for each bytes chunk. The decoder will hold partial bytes internally; at the end of the stream you must call decoder.decode(b'', final=True) to flush any buffered bytes. This approach preserves correctness without requiring lookahead or complex boundary logic.

documents.content: A practical pattern is: open the source in binary mode, read fixed-size blocks (for example CHUNK_SIZE = 8192 bytes) with f.read(CHUNK_SIZE), and feed those byte blocks to an incremental UTF-8 decoder. For example, instantiate decoder = codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')() then in the loop do text_part = decoder.decode(block); append text_part to the output string or write it to a text sink. The decoder buffers partial characters automatically so callers need not handle split code points. As an alternative convenience, io.TextIOWrapper can wrap a binary stream and present a text interface with buffering and decoding handled internally; however, explicit incremental decoding gives control over chunking and when to flush using decoder.decode(b'', final=True).

documents.content: UTF-8 has a history stretching from early Unicode debates; older systems used fixed-width encodings like UTF-16, and some file formats include a byte-order mark (BOM) which can complicate detection. Some developers mention codecs.iterdecode() as a convenience iterator that decodes an iterable of byte chunks, and third-party libraries offer streaming helpers. Benchmarks sometimes quote throughput numbers for decoding thousands of megabytes per second, but those figures depend heavily on CPU, memory bandwidth, and whether validation is strict. task_row_model.golden_answer: Open the source in binary mode and read fixed-size byte blocks (e.g., f.read(CHUNK_SIZE)). Create an incremental UTF-8 decoder with codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')(), call decoder.decode(block) for each chunk and append the returned text. After the loop call decoder.decode(b'', final=True) to flush any buffered partial bytes. The decoder buffers incomplete multibyte sequences, preventing decode errors.
